content.content:
1	# Real-world Event Decision Simulator
2	
3	A small backend foundation for an emergency-response and logistics decision simulation platform. The service exposes a public HTTP entry point that future features can extend without changing the startup contract.
4	
5	## Run
6	
7	Requires Python 3.11 or newer and has no third-party runtime dependencies.
8	
9	```bash
10	python -m event_sim serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
11	```
12	
13	Check the public health endpoint:
14	
15	```bash
16	curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
17	```
18	
19	## Test
20	
21	```bash
22	python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
23	```
24	
25	## Public interface
26	
27	- `GET /health` returns JSON with the service name and `ok` status, under the keys `service` and `status`: `{"service": "real-world-event-decision-sim", "status": "ok"}`.
28	- Unknown paths return a JSON `not_found` error with HTTP 404.
29	- `python -m event_sim --help` documents the command-line entry point.
30	
31	## Credentials and organization isolation
32	
33	Every entry point except `GET /health` and the credential registration entry
34	point requires a request-scoped Bearer credential. Credentials are held only
35	in the server process: restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with an
36	empty credential registry, and an unregistered token reaches nothing.
37	
38	### `POST /auth/tokens`
39	
40	The one entry point that requires no credential. Requires
41	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with exactly
42	these three fields, in any order:
43	
44	| Field            | Rule                                  |
45	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- |
46	| `token`          | non-empty string                      |
47	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                      |
48	| `role`           | one of `read` or `write`              |
49	
50	- `201 Created` — new token registered. The body echoes the three fields as
51	  compact JSON with keys sorted by code point and one trailing newline:
52	  `{"organizationId":"org-1","role":"write","token":"tok-1"}\n`.
53	- `200 OK` — the same token was resubmitted with the identical organization
54	  and role; it is not registered a second time and the same body is echoed.
55	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "auth_conflict"}`) — the token is already bound
56	  to a different organization or role. The binding is never rewritten.
57	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
58	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
59	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
60	  missing/extra field, a blank or non-string `token`/`organizationId`, or a
61	  `role` other than `read`/`write`. No record is stored.
62	
63	```bash
64	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/auth/tokens \
65	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
66	  -d '{"token":"tok-1","organizationId":"org-1","role":"write"}'
67	```
68	
69	### Bearer authentication
70	
71	All other requests carry the registered token in an
72	`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. A missing header, a non-Bearer
73	scheme, a malformed bearer value, or an unregistered token yields
74	`401 Unauthorized` with `{"error": "unauthorized"}`.
75	
76	A valid credential that acts outside its bound organization or role yields
77	`403 Forbidden` with `{"error": "forbidden"}` and performs no write. The
78	`organizationId` in any request parameter or body field must equal the
79	token's registered organization; reading or writing another organization's
80	data is forbidden.
81	
82	- A `read` token may call only the state-free query and decision-computation
83	  entry points: the event list, aggregate, region, and replay (including
84	  replay comparison and replay decision) queries, the reservation/alert
85	  listings,
86	  `GET /branches/{branchId}/resources`,
87	  `GET /branches/{branchId}/events/replay/decisions`,
88	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/resources`,
89	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/reservations`,
90	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events`,
91	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/region`,
92	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/aggregate`,
93	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/region/aggregate`,
94	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/replay/decisions`,
95	  `POST /decisions/evaluate`, `POST /decisions/allocate`,
96	  `POST /branches/compare`, `POST /branches/compare/events`,
97	  `POST /branches/compare/reservations`,
98	  `POST /branches/compare/resources`, `POST /snapshots/compare`,
99	  `POST /snapshots/compare/events`,
100	  `POST /snapshots/compare/reservations`,
101	  `POST /snapshots/compare/resources`,
102	  `POST /snapshots/{snapshotId}/decisions/evaluate`, and the other
103	  read-only branch entry points.
104	- Committing an event or reservation, evaluating an alert, and creating a
105	  snapshot or branch are writes; only a `write` token may call them. A
106	  `read` token against a write entry point receives `403`. The authorization
107	  decision and the ledger/inventory mutation complete under one lock, so a
108	  rejected request never changes the ledger or inventory.
109	
110	Snapshots and branches belong to the organization that created them. A
111	snapshot captures only that organization's events, resource capacities, and
112	reservations, and the three summary counts count only that organization; a
113	branch forks only a snapshot owned by the same organization, and branch entry
114	points authenticate with the same rules as the main service. Snapshot and
115	branch names are unique across the whole service (not merely within one
116	organization), and accessing another organization's snapshot or branch by name
117	is `403`, never `404`.
118	
119	## Event ledger
120	
121	Events are held only in the server process: restarting (or starting a new
122	instance) begins with an empty ledger.
123	
124	### `POST /events`
125	
126	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with
127	exactly these five top-level fields:
128	
129	| Field          | Rule                                      |
130	| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
131	| `eventId`      | non-empty string                          |
132	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                        |
133	| `type`         | non-empty string                          |
134	| `occurredAt`   | non-negative integer (no floats, no booleans) |
135	| `payload`      | JSON object                               |
136	
137	```bash
138	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/events \
139	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
140	  -d '{"eventId":"evt-1","organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","occurredAt":100,"payload":{"severity":"low"}}'
141	```
142	
143	- `201 Created` — new event stored; the response is the same five-field JSON.
144	- `200 OK` — the same `eventId` was resubmitted with identical fields; the
145	  stored event is returned and nothing is added.
146	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "event_id_conflict"}`) — the `eventId` exists but
147	  the other fields differ.
148	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
149	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
150	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — fields are missing, extra, or invalid
151	  (arrays at the top level, blank identifiers, floats, etc.).
152	
153	### `GET /events?organizationId=...`
154	
155	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
156	Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
157	belong only to that organization and are sorted by `occurredAt`, then
158	`eventId`. An unknown organization returns `"events": []`. A missing, blank, or
159	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
160	
161	### `GET /events/aggregate?organizationId=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
162	
163	Counts stored events per time window, without modifying the ledger. Only
164	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted; other
165	organizations' data is never included.
166	
167	Query parameters:
168	
169	| Parameter        | Rule                                                                 |
170	| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
171	| `organizationId` | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
172	| `type`           | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
173	| `windowSize`     | required exactly once, positive integer text (e.g. `60`)             |
174	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
175	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
176	
177	`from` and `to` must be omitted together or supplied together, and must
178	satisfy `from <= to`. A missing, duplicated, or invalid parameter yields
179	`422` with a JSON body containing a stable `error` field.
180	
181	Windows start at `0` and each covers `[start, end)` with
182	`end = start + windowSize`; an event belongs to a window when
183	`start <= occurredAt < end`. The `200` response is:
184	
185	```json
186	{
187	  "organizationId": "org-1",
188	  "type": "incident.created",
189	  "windowSize": 60,
190	  "from": null,
191	  "to": null,
192	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
193	}
194	```
195	
196	- Without `from`/`to` (`from` and `to` echo back as `null`), only windows
197	  actually covered by matching events are returned; with no matching events
198	  `windows` is `[]`.
199	- With `from`/`to`, only events with `from <= occurredAt <= to` are counted,
200	  and every window intersecting the closed interval `[from, to]` is returned,
201	  including empty windows with `count: 0`.
202	- `windows` is sorted by `start` ascending; results are deterministic
203	  regardless of event insertion order, replays, or identical timestamps.
204	
205	```bash
206	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
207	```
208	
209	### Region attribution
210	
211	An event's region is the value of the `region` key in its `payload`. Only a
212	non-empty string attributes an event to a region: a missing key, an empty
213	string, or a non-string value means the event has no region. Region values
214	are matched verbatim (exact comparison, no trimming or normalization), and
215	regions need no registration — an unknown region simply matches zero events
216	and is never implicitly created. The region endpoints below are read-only:
217	they never write the event ledger, reservations, or alerts.
218	
219	### `GET /events/region?organizationId=...&region=...`
220	
221	Lists one organization's events attributed to one region. Both
222	`organizationId` and `region` must appear exactly once and be non-empty; a
223	missing, duplicated, or blank parameter yields `422`. Returns `200` with
224	`{"organizationId": "...", "region": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
225	are sorted by `occurredAt`, then `eventId`, exactly like `GET /events`. An
226	unknown organization or region returns `"events": []`; other organizations'
227	events are never included. The body is compact JSON with keys sorted by code
228	point and a trailing newline.
229	
230	```bash
231	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region?organizationId=org-1&region=north'
232	```
233	
234	### `GET /events/region/aggregate?organizationId=...&region=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
235	
236	Counts per time window, using the exact same parameter rules, window
237	boundaries, ordering, and `from`/`to` semantics as
238	`GET /events/aggregate`, with an added `region` parameter that must appear
239	exactly once and be non-empty. Only events matching the organization,
240	region, and type are counted; events without a non-empty string payload
241	`region` never match. The `200` response mirrors the aggregate response with
242	one added `region` key (compact JSON, keys sorted by code point, trailing
243	newline):
244	
245	```json
246	{
247	  "organizationId": "org-1",
248	  "region": "north",
249	  "type": "incident.created",
250	  "windowSize": 60,
251	  "from": null,
252	  "to": null,
253	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
254	}
255	```
256	
257	Without a range, only windows covered by matching events are returned; an
258	unknown region behaves like a zero-event match. With a range, every window
259	intersecting `[from, to]` is returned, including empty ones. Any parameter
260	problem — missing, duplicated, or blank values, a non-positive-integer
261	`windowSize`, unpaired or non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to` — yields
262	`422` with `{"error": "validation_error", ...}`.
263	
264	```bash
265	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&region=north&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
266	```
267	
268	### `GET /events/replay/decisions?organizationId=...&type=...&windowSize=...&threshold=...`
269	
270	A read-only, step-by-step recomputation of the window counts and peak
271	decision as matching events enter a replay one at a time. The ledger,
272	reservation inventory, and alerts are never written; identical requests
273	return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write` credentials
274	may call it. The query parameters are:
275	
276	| Parameter        | Rule                                                                 |
277	| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
278	| `organizationId` | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
279	| `type`           | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
280	| `windowSize`     | required exactly once, positive integer text (e.g. `60`)             |
281	| `threshold`      | required exactly once, positive integer text (e.g. `3`)              |
282	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
283	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
284	
285	`from` and `to` must be omitted together or supplied together, and must
286	satisfy `from <= to`. A missing, duplicated, blank, or invalid parameter
287	yields `422` with `validation_error`.
288	
289	Only events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are replayed; other
290	organizations' data never enters the result. The matching events are
291	ordered by `occurredAt` ascending and then `eventId` in Unicode code-point
292	order, and accumulated into the replay in that order. Each replay step
293	reports the event's `eventId` and `occurredAt`, the window-count rows for
294	every event accumulated up to and including that one, and the peak decision
295	at that point. Windows start at `0` and each covers
296	`[start, start + windowSize)`:
297	
298	- Without `from`/`to`, only windows actually covered by the accumulated
299	  events appear.
300	- With `from`/`to`, events outside the closed interval `[from, to]` still
301	  arrive as replay steps in order, but every window intersecting the
302	  interval is returned at every step, including empty windows with
303	  `count: 0`, exactly like the ranged aggregate.
304	- The peak is the largest window count; ties resolve to the earliest
305	  start. `action` is `"escalate"` when the peak reaches `threshold` and
306	  `"observe"` otherwise. With no matching events there are no steps at
307	  all; a step whose accumulated prefix has no counted window carries
308	  `peakCount: 0`, `peakStart: null`, and `"observe"`.
309	
310	At each step the window rows are exactly what `GET /events/aggregate`
311	returns on the accumulated prefix and the peak fields are exactly what
312	`POST /decisions/evaluate` returns on it. The `200` response echoes the
313	organization, type, window width, threshold, and the (possibly null)
314	range, and carries the ordered `steps` array. It is compact JSON with
315	keys sorted by code point, integer values kept as integers, and one
316	trailing newline:
317	
318	```json
319	{"from":null,"organizationId":"org-1","steps":[{"action":"observe","eventId":"evt-d","occurredAt":0,"peakCount":1,"peakStart":0,"windows":[{"count":1,"end":60,"start":0}]},{"action":"observe","eventId":"evt-c","occurredAt":100,"peakCount":1,"peakStart":0,"windows":[{"count":1,"end":60,"start":0},{"count":1,"end":120,"start":60}]}],"threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60}
320	```
321	
322	```bash
323	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/replay/decisions?organizationId=org-1&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&threshold=3&from=0&to=180' \
324	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1'
325	```
326	
327	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
328	  is missing, malformed, or not registered; the body carries no business
329	  content.
330	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a parameter is missing,
331	  duplicated, or blank, `windowSize`/`threshold` is not a positive integer,
332	  `from`/`to` are unpaired or non-integer, or `from > to`.
333	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the parameter's
334	  organization differs from the credential's. An unknown organization
335	  registered to the caller computes as zero events and returns normally;
336	  a failed request leaves no trace.
337	
338	### `POST /decisions/evaluate`
339	
340	A read-only, deterministic emergency decision over the same windows as the
341	aggregate endpoint. The ledger is never written to or changed by a decision
342	request. Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON
343	object containing exactly these fields:
344	
345	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
346	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
347	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
348	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
349	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
350	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
351	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
352	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
353	
354	Only events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted. Windows
355	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`. Without `from`/`to`,
356	only windows actually covered by matching events are considered; with a
357	range, events are filtered by the closed interval `from <= occurredAt <= to`
358	and every window intersecting that interval is considered, including empty
359	ones for audit reconciliation.
360	
361	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
362	
363	```json
364	{
365	  "organizationId": "org-1",
366	  "type": "incident.created",
367	  "windowSize": 60,
368	  "from": null,
369	  "to": null,
370	  "peakStart": 60,
371	  "peakCount": 2,
372	  "action": "observe"
373	}
374	```
375	
376	- `peakCount` is the largest window count and `peakStart` is that window's
377	  start; ties resolve to the earliest start, so results are reproducible
378	  regardless of event submission order.
379	- With no matching events (or no non-empty windows in range), `peakCount` is
380	  `0`, `peakStart` is `null`, and `action` is `"observe"`.
381	- `action` is `"escalate"` when `peakCount >= threshold`, otherwise
382	  `"observe"`.
383	- Unknown organizations or types compute as zero events and return normally;
384	  other organizations' data is never included.
385	
386	```bash
387	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/evaluate \
388	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
389	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
390	```
391	
392	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
393	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no decision is
394	  produced.
395	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
396	  invalid types, unpaired `from`/`to`, or out-of-range values.
397	
398	### `POST /decisions/allocate`
399	
400	A read-only, deterministic resource plan computed entirely from the request
401	body. Nothing is written to the event ledger, no earlier plan is inherited,
402	and concurrent requests cannot affect each other. Requires
403	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object containing
404	exactly these fields:
405	
406	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
407	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
408	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
409	| `demands`        | required array (may be empty) of demand objects              |
410	| `resources`      | required array (may be empty) of resource objects            |
411	
412	A demand object has exactly `demandId` (non-empty string, unique within the
413	request), `units` (positive integer), and `priority` (non-negative integer).
414	A resource object has exactly `resourceId` (non-empty string, unique within
415	the request) and `capacity` (positive integer). Booleans, floats, negative or
416	zero values where a positive integer is required, wrong element types, blank
417	or duplicate identifiers, and unknown fields are all rejected.
418	
419	Demands are handled by `priority` descending; ties resolve by `demandId` in
420	Unicode code-point order. A demand is placed wholly into the
421	lexicographically smallest `resourceId` whose remaining capacity covers its
422	units, and that capacity is deducted immediately. Demands are never split and
423	capacity is never oversold; a demand that fits in no remaining resource goes
424	to `unassigned` — priorities and units are never adjusted to place more
425	demands.
426	
427	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
428	
429	```json
430	{
431	  "organizationId": "org-1",
432	  "assignments": [
433	    {"demandId": "d-a", "resourceId": "r-a", "units": 2},
434	    {"demandId": "d-b", "resourceId": "r-b", "units": 4}
435	  ],
436	  "unassigned": ["d-big"],
437	  "totalUnits": 6
438	}
439	```
440	
441	- `assignments` lists `{"demandId", "resourceId", "units"}` objects in
442	  processing order.
443	- `unassigned` lists the demandIds that could not be placed, sorted by
444	  `demandId`.
445	- `totalUnits` counts only units that were assigned.
446	- Empty `demands`/`resources` arrays are valid and return empty results;
447	  identical submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON.
448	
449	```bash
450	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/allocate \
451	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
452	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","demands":[{"demandId":"d-a","units":2,"priority":1}],"resources":[{"resourceId":"r-a","capacity":5}]}'
453	```
454	
455	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
456	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
457	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
458	  invalid types, duplicate or blank identifiers, or out-of-range values.
459	
460	## Reservation inventory
461	
462	Reservations are held only in the server process alongside the event ledger:
463	restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with empty inventory. The
464	first reservation that names a resource fixes that resource's capacity; it
465	is never rewritten afterwards.
466	
467	### `POST /reservations`
468	
469	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
470	with exactly these five top-level fields:
471	
472	| Field           | Rule                                      |
473	| --------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
474	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                         |
475	| `reservationId` | non-empty string                          |
476	| `resourceId`    | non-empty string                          |
477	| `quantity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
478	| `capacity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
479	
480	```bash
481	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reservations \
482	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
483	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a","quantity":2,"capacity":5}'
484	```
485	
486	A successful response is compact JSON with stable key order, integer values,
487	and a trailing newline:
488	
489	```json
490	{"capacity":5,"occupied":2,"organizationId":"org-1","quantity":2,"remaining":3,"reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a"}
491	```
492	
493	`occupied` is the total confirmed quantity on the resource and `remaining`
494	is `capacity - occupied`; the balance can never go negative because the
495	check and the deduction commit atomically under one lock, so concurrent
496	requests cannot oversell a resource or lose each other's writes.
497	
498	- `201 Created` — new reservation committed; the first reservation for a
499	  resource also establishes its capacity.
500	- `200 OK` — the same `reservationId` was resubmitted with identical fields;
501	  nothing is counted twice and the balances are unchanged.
502	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "reservation_conflict"}`) — the `reservationId`
503	  exists but the other fields differ.
504	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_conflict"}`) — the resource already
505	  has a recorded capacity and the declared `capacity` differs; the recorded
506	  capacity is never rewritten.
507	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_exceeded"}`) — the quantity exceeds
508	  the resource's remaining balance; inventory and existing reservations are
509	  unchanged.
510	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
511	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no reservation
512	  is produced.
513	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
514	  blank or non-string identifiers, or non-positive/non-integer values.
515	
516	### `GET /reservations?organizationId=...`
517	
518	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
519	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "reservations":
520	[...]}` containing only that organization's reservations, sorted by
521	`resourceId` then `reservationId` in Unicode code-point order. Each entry
522	carries `quantity`, the resource's `capacity`, and the resource-wide
523	`occupied` and `remaining` balances. An unknown organization returns
524	`"reservations": []`. A missing, blank, or duplicated parameter yields
525	`422`.
526	
527	## Alert suppression and escalation
528	
529	Alerts are held only in the main service process alongside the event
530	ledger; restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with no alerts.
531	Snapshots and branches never capture alerts, and the alert entry points
532	exist only on the main service — no `/branches/{branchId}/alerts/...`
533	paths are added.
534	
535	### `POST /alerts/evaluate`
536	
537	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
538	containing exactly these fields:
539	
540	| Field               | Rule                                                          |
541	| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
542	| `organizationId`    | required, non-empty string                                   |
543	| `type`              | required, non-empty string                                   |
544	| `windowSize`        | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
545	| `threshold`         | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
546	| `suppressionWindow` | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
547	| `from`              | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
548	| `to`                | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
549	
550	The peak uses the exact same windowing as `POST /decisions/evaluate`: only
551	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted, windows
552	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`, ties resolve to the
553	earliest window start, and an unknown organization or type computes as
554	zero events. The event ledger is never modified.
555	
556	- When the peak is below the threshold, `action` is `"observe"`, no alert
557	  is written, `alertId` is `null`, and `suppressedCount` is `null`.
558	- When the peak reaches the threshold, the peak start is compared with the
559	  most recent prior alert for the same organization and type:
560	  - `peakStart` not earlier than the prior start and at least
561	    `suppressionWindow` away (`peakStart - priorStart >=
562	    suppressionWindow`) creates a new alert; `action` is `"escalate"`,
563	    `alertId` is the new id (`alert-1`, `alert-2`, …, one global sequence
564	    across all organizations and types), and `suppressedCount` is `0`.
565	  - A peak start less than `suppressionWindow` after the prior alert's
566	    peak start increments that alert's suppression count instead; `action`
567	    is `"suppress"`, `alertId` is the prior alert's id, and
568	    `suppressedCount` is the new total. The first threshold hit for an
569	    organization/type always creates an alert.
570	
571	The suppression decision and the alert creation commit atomically under
572	one lock, so concurrent threshold hits cannot both open alerts or suppress
573	against a stale view. The `200` response echoes every request parameter
574	and adds the result fields (compact JSON, stable key order, integer values,
575	trailing newline):
576	
577	```json
578	{"action":"escalate","alertId":"alert-1","from":null,"organizationId":"org-1","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60,"suppressedCount":0,"suppressionWindow":120,"threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60}
579	```
580	
581	```bash
582	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/alerts/evaluate \
583	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
584	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3,"suppressionWindow":120}'
585	```
586	
587	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
588	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no alert is
589	  written.
590	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
591	  blank or non-string identifiers, booleans/floats where integers are
592	  required, non-positive values, unpaired `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
593	
594	### `GET /alerts?organizationId=...`
595	
596	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
597	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "alerts": [...]}`
598	containing only that organization's alerts. Each entry carries `alertId`,
599	`type`, `peakStart`, `threshold`, and `suppressedCount`, sorted by
600	`peakStart` ascending and then `alertId` in Unicode code-point order. An
601	unknown organization returns `"alerts": []`. A missing, blank, or
602	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
603	
604	## Snapshots and branches
605	
606	Snapshots capture the current main service state under a unique name so that
607	decisions can later be recomputed against that exact state. Branches fork a
608	snapshot into an isolated copy that supports the existing event, aggregate,
609	decision, and reservation entry points without sharing any mutable state with
610	the main service or with other branches.
611	
612	### Organization boundaries
613	
614	Every snapshot and branch is owned by the organization of the `write`
615	credential that created it, and all capture, naming, and visibility rules are
616	scoped to that boundary:
617	
618	- A snapshot captures **only the creator's own organization** — its events,
619	  the capacities of resources it reserves, and its reservations. Other
620	  organizations' events, reservation identifiers, and capacity records are
621	  neither captured nor summarized. The three counts in the response
622	  (`events`, `resources`, `reservations`) count only that organization. Two
623	  snapshots created from the same state return identical counts; another
624	  organization's data never changes them.
625	- A branch forked from a snapshot carries only that snapshot organization's
626	  data. Inside the branch, event and reservation names are compared only
627	  against that organization's own records. Another organization's event
628	  identifiers, reservation identifiers, and capacity records never cause a
629	  branch commit to conflict and never affect a branch balance.
630	- Snapshot and branch names are **unique across the whole service** and are
631	  owned by the creator's organization. A duplicate name conflicts regardless
632	  of which organization holds it: creating a snapshot with a name already in
633	  use returns `409` `snapshot_conflict` (the original snapshot is never
634	  rewritten), and creating a branch with a name already in use returns `409`
635	  `branch_conflict` (the existing branch is untouched). Names are not
636	  namespaced per organization.
637	- Using another organization's **snapshot name as a fork source**, or reading
638	  another organization's **branch by name**, returns `403 Forbidden`
639	  (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) with no content, even though the name exists. A
640	  name that has never appeared anywhere is the only case that yields `404`:
641	  a missing snapshot is `snapshot_not_found` and a missing branch is
642	  `branch_not_found`. Missing objects are never implicitly created.
643	- When creating a branch, snapshot ownership (`403`) is decided before the
644	  duplicate branch name (`409`); a foreign snapshot is forbidden even if the
645	  requested `branchId` is also taken. The snapshot list (`GET /snapshots`)
646	  and branch summaries are visible only within the owning organization.
647	- Authorization and the write happen under one lock for alert evaluation,
648	  snapshot creation, and branch creation alike. A rejected request leaves no
649	  alert, snapshot, or branch behind, and concurrent creations of the same
650	  name have exactly one winner; the loser receives the conflict response.
651	
652	Snapshots and branches capture only events, resource capacities, and
653	reservations — alerts are never captured, and the alert entry points remain
654	main-only with no branch-prefixed sub-paths. Like everything else here,
655	snapshots and branches live only in the server process and are cleared on
656	restart; there is no persistence, authorization, or replay across restarts.

658	### `POST /snapshots`
659	
660	Requires a `write` credential and `Content-Type: application/json`. The body
661	must be a JSON object containing exactly one field:
662	
663	| Field        | Rule                     |
664	| ------------ | ------------------------ |
665	| `snapshotId` | non-empty string         |
666	
667	The snapshot is owned by the caller's organization and captures only that
668	organization's state. A successful response is `201` with compact integer
669	JSON and one trailing newline, matching the byte contract of the other write
670	entry points:
671	
672	```json
673	{"events":2,"reservations":1,"resources":1,"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
674	```
675	
676	- `events`, `resources`, and `reservations` count the creator organization's
677	  captured events, distinct resources with a recorded capacity, and
678	  reservations; other organizations' data is never counted.
679	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "snapshot_conflict"}`) — the name already exists
680	  anywhere in the service (held by any organization); the original snapshot
681	  content is never replaced or mutated.
682	- `403 Forbidden` — the credential is read-only or acts outside its
683	  organization; no snapshot is stored.
684	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
685	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
686	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, a missing or extra field,
687	  a blank value, or a non-string `snapshotId`.
688	- Any failed request leaves both the main state and existing snapshots
689	  unchanged.

699	### `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/resources?organizationId=...`

703	`POST /snapshots/compare/resources`, computed from the exact same balance

705	or in the main service is read for mutation or written: the main-service

1142	  events appear.
1143	- With `from`/`to`, events outside the closed interval `[from, to]` still
1144	  arrive as replay steps in order, but every window intersecting the
1145	  interval is returned at every step, including empty windows with
1146	  `count: 0`, exactly like the ranged aggregate.
1147	- The peak is the largest window count; ties resolve to the earliest
1148	  start. `action` is `"escalate"` when the peak reaches `threshold` and
1149	  `"observe"` otherwise. With no matching events there are no steps at
1150	  all; a step whose accumulated prefix has no counted window carries
1151	  `peakCount: 0`, `peakStart: null`, and `"observe"`.
1152	
1153	At each step the window rows are exactly what
1154	`GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/aggregate` returns on the accumulated
1155	prefix and the peak fields are exactly what
1156	`POST /snapshots/{snapshotId}/decisions/evaluate` returns on it. The `200`
1157	response echoes the organization, snapshot, type, window width, threshold,
1158	and the (possibly null) range, and carries the ordered `steps` array. It is
1159	compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer values kept as
1160	integers, and one trailing newline:
1161	
1162	```json
1163	{"from":null,"organizationId":"org-1","snapshotId":"snap-1","steps":[{"action":"observe","eventId":"evt-d","occurredAt":0,"peakCount":1,"peakStart":0,"windows":[{"count":1,"end":60,"start":0}]}],"threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60}
1164	```
1165	
1166	```bash
1167	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/snap-1/events/replay/decisions?organizationId=org-1&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&threshold=3&from=0&to=180' \
1168	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1'
1169	```
1170	
1171	The verdict order is fixed: the credential is checked first, then the query
1172	shape, then the organization, and only then the snapshot name.
1173	
1174	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
1175	  is missing, malformed, or not registered; the body carries no business
1176	  content.
1177	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a parameter is missing,
1178	  duplicated, blank, or invalid: a non-positive-integer
1179	  `windowSize`/`threshold`, unpaired or non-integer `from`/`to`, or
1180	  `from > to`.
1181	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the parameter's
1182	  organization differs from the credential's, or the named snapshot
1183	  belongs to another organization.
1184	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — the snapshot name
1185	  has never existed; a replay never implicitly creates a snapshot.
1186	
1187	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed request creates no
1188	snapshot and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
1189	
1190	### `POST /snapshots/{snapshotId}/decisions/evaluate`
1191	
1192	A read-only peak decision over one snapshot's captured events for the
1193	caller's organization — the single-snapshot counterpart of the two-snapshot
1194	window decision (`POST /snapshots/compare`), lowering the exact window and
1195	peak contract of `POST /decisions/evaluate` onto the events the snapshot
1196	captured at its creation time. Snapshots are immutable, so nothing in the
1197	snapshot, in any branch, or in the main service is read for mutation or
1198	written: the main-service event ledger, reservation inventory, and alert
1199	state are untouched, failed requests leave no trace, and identical requests
1200	return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write` credentials
1201	may call it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a
1202	JSON object containing exactly these fields:
1203	
1204	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
1205	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1206	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
1207	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
1208	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
1209	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
1210	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
1211	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
1212	
1213	`from` and `to` must be omitted together or supplied together, and must
1214	satisfy `from <= to`. Only the snapshot's captured events matching both the
1215	caller's organization and `type` are counted; other organizations' data and
1216	events committed after capture never enter the result.
1217	
1218	Windows start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)` — boundaries
1219	identical to the main decision and the snapshot window comparison. Without
1220	`from`/`to`, only windows actually covered by matching captured events are
1221	considered; with a range, captured events are filtered by the closed
1222	interval `from <= occurredAt <= to` and every window intersecting that
1223	interval is considered, including empty ones counted as zero. The `200`
1224	response echoes the organization, snapshot, type, window width and the
1225	(possibly null) time range, and adds the peak result:
1226	
1227	```json
1228	{
1229	  "organizationId": "org-1",
1230	  "snapshotId": "snap-1",
1231	  "type": "incident.created",
1232	  "windowSize": 60,
1233	  "from": null,
1234	  "to": null,
1235	  "peakStart": 60,
1236	  "peakCount": 2,
1237	  "action": "observe"
1238	}
1239	```
1240	
1241	- `peakCount` is the largest window count and `peakStart` is that window's
1242	  start; ties resolve to the earliest start, so results are reproducible
1243	  regardless of event submission order.
1244	- With no matching events, `peakCount` is `0`, `peakStart` is `null`, and
1245	  `action` is `"observe"`.
1246	- `action` is `"escalate"` when `peakCount >= threshold`, otherwise
1247	  `"observe"`.
1248	- Because the peak shares the window comparison's contract, comparing a
1249	  snapshot with itself via `POST /snapshots/compare` reports this exact
1250	  `peakStart`, `peakCount`, and `action` on both the `left` and `right`
1251	  decision sides, item by item.
1252	
1253	The response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer values
1254	kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
1255	
1256	```json
1257	{"action":"observe","from":null,"organizationId":"org-1","peakCount":2,"peakStart":60,"snapshotId":"snap-1","to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60}
1258	```
1259	
1260	```bash
1261	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/snap-1/decisions/evaluate \
1262	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
1263	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
1264	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
1265	```
1266	
1267	The verdict order is fixed: the credential is checked first, then the
1268	request body, then the organization, and only then the snapshot name.
1269	
1270	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
1271	  is missing, malformed, or not registered; the body carries no business
1272	  content.
1273	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
1274	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
1275	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
1276	  missing or extra field, a blank or non-string `organizationId`/`type`,
1277	  booleans/floats where integers are required, non-positive
1278	  `windowSize`/`threshold`, unpaired or non-integer `from`/`to`, or
1279	  `from > to`. No snapshot is created and nothing is written.
1280	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the body's organization
1281	  differs from the credential's, or the named snapshot belongs to another
1282	  organization.
1283	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — the snapshot name
1284	  has never existed; an evaluation never implicitly creates a snapshot.
1285	
1286	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed request creates no
1287	snapshot and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
1288	
1289	### `POST /branches`
1290	
1291	Requires a `write` credential and `Content-Type: application/json`. The body
1292	must be a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
1293	
1294	| Field        | Rule                     |
1295	| ------------ | ------------------------ |
1296	| `branchId`   | non-empty string         |
1297	| `snapshotId` | non-empty string         |
1298	
1299	The new branch receives independent copies of the snapshot's events,
1300	resource capacities, and reservation balances (which hold only the snapshot
1301	owner organization's data).
1302	
1303	- `201 Created` — the branch summary is returned:
1304	
1305	```json
1306	{"branchId":"br-1","events":2,"reservations":1,"resources":1,"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
1307	```
1308	
1309	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the named snapshot exists but
1310	  belongs to another organization (ownership is checked before the branch
1311	  name), or the credential is read-only. No branch is created and no snapshot
1312	  content is returned.
1313	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — no snapshot with that
1314	  name has ever existed; no branch is created.
1315	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "branch_conflict"}`) — the snapshot is owned by
1316	  the caller but a branch with that `branchId` already exists anywhere in the
1317	  service. The existing branch is unaffected.
1318	- `415`, `400`, and `422` follow the same rules as other JSON write
1319	  endpoints; `422` (`validation_error`) covers missing, extra, blank, or
1320	  non-string fields.
1321	
1322	### `GET /branches/{branchId}`
1323	
1324	Returns `200` with the branch summary (see above) when the branch belongs to
1325	the caller's organization. A branch owned by another organization returns
1326	`403` with `{"error": "forbidden"}` and no content. Only a branch name that
1327	has never existed returns `404` with `{"error": "branch_not_found"}`.
1328	
1329	### Branch-prefixed entry points
1330	
1331	A known branch exposes the existing endpoints under
1332	`/branches/{branchId}/...`, with identical request contracts, query
1333	validation, ordering, and window semantics:
1334	
1335	| Method | Path                                      | Effect                                    |
1336	| ------ | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
